articles.que_paso: A Greece-based cybersecurity researcher, Vangelis Stykas, has been tracking North Korean hackers for almost two years, gaining access to their systems and uncovering the extent of their global hacking operations. The researcher has been analyzing the hackers' command-and-control servers and has identified numerous companies and organizations that have been impacted by the hacking operations. The discovery sheds light on the sophisticated and widespread nature of North Korea's cyber attacks.
datos: 1,640 companies across 57 countries have been impacted by North Korea's hacking operations
700 to 800 of the impacted organizations have had 'really damaging' intrusions
5 terabytes of data have been accessed by the researcher
Vangelis Stykas gained access to North Korean systems 22 months ago
Around a dozen impacted companies will be publicly named by Stykas, including Boston Children’s Hospital, AEON Smart Technology, and Coinbase
The hacking operations have been found to have 'root access' to servers, AWS, and blockchain access in some cases
articles.conclusion: The findings highlight the significant threat posed by North Korea's hacking operations to companies and organizations worldwide, emphasizing the need for robust cybersecurity measures to prevent such breaches. The research also demonstrates the importance of collaboration between cybersecurity experts and affected organizations in identifying and mitigating these threats.
